rv.q: “A seamless theatrical experience, this beguiling, virtually sung-through musical is notable for the expressive beauty of its score, the dark imagination of its stage pictures and the clarity of its storytelling.

It feels like the most relevant and resistant musical in town but it never comes off as shrill or moving in some kind of dull lockstep with all the other self-aware plays and musicals lamenting Trump’s America by playing tritely to the choir, critics and all.
The poignant, enchanting story this powerful duo brings to Broadway is notable mostly for its memorable music and especially haunting lyrics.
After 'Hamilton,' 'Hadestown' is the best new musical on Broadway, period.

Hadestown, the most thrilling new original musical of the season, is taking on the great grandfolk of all mythology, sending Orpheus and Eurydice straight to Hades via the irresistible rhythms of New Orleans jazz, sultry French Quarter gyrations and a cast no pantheon could have improved.
Arriving on Broadway with its earthly delights more or less intact, this perfectly heavenly musical — with book, music and lyrics by Anaïs Mitchell — should stick around for a while.
Hadestown, moment after lovely moment, sweeps you up in its atmospherics and in the intensity of its eco-Marxist vision of solidarity and the liberating potential of art.

The gods, or more likely Ms. Chavkin and her creative team, have saved “Hadestown” on its way uptown — via Edmonton and London — by turning it into something very much warmer, if not yet ideally warm.
His guitarist-on-a-stool bit sums up the overriding problem of “Hadestown,” which turns one of the world’s greatest love stories into a concert at the back of a West Village wine bar.
Yet “Hadestown” never fulfills that essential mandate — revealing why a jazzy adaptation of Orpheus and Eurydice’s story should merit all this muscular stomping around.
Hadestown is probably the most exciting musical to be seen in New York at present with its all-inclusive staging, ingenious design, classic story and colorful score in various styles and genres.
And while this free-wheeling version of the Orpheus myth may not appeal to everyone, it is a collaborative tour de force.
I happily raise my cup to this sublime evening of musical theater.
I'm happy to report that all the changes accomplished something of a miracle.
Quite possibly the most exciting new musical of the Broadway season...It also takes the nod for most-improved new musical.
It’s not a punishment, it’s a reward with great music, incredible voices, some wonderful performances, and a surprising love story.
What made Hadestown most thrilling remains – the delightful score, which mixes sweet and sexy folk, rocking jazz, and exquisite blues.
This entrancing, romantic new musical has taken a long road to get to the Theatre.
More often than not, 'Hadestown' is exciting, compelling and beautiful.
Friends, countrymen, whoever –get thee down to the Theatre where Anais Mitchell’s incredibly moving and melodic musical, “Hadestown,” is burning up the stage, bursting with ingenuity and intensity.
Going to hell has never been as much fun as seeing a performance of Anaïs Mitchell's musical Hadestown.
The result is a stylish, resonant, high-energy musical, much fuller than the Off Broadway version at Theater Workshop in 2016.

If there is more darkness than light in Hadestown, there’s also a tender love story—two, in fact, one ending on a more hopeful note than you might expect—and songs and performances that will lift mortal spirits, from wherever they lurk.
Whatever devil's bargains were made, it's good to see Hadestown has kept its soul in the process.
It's beautifully conceived, executed, and staged in a most unusual way.
Chavkin, her production team and cast are working at the top of their form — and they go a long way to masking some of the show’s shortcomings.
The Broadway show takes on its own strong persona while drawing life from the roots that support it.

"Looks and sounds terrific, and yet it lacks something vital...The show is brilliantly staged and designed, and there’s no denying the infernal red-hot charms of the...score...There’s too little heat to the young couple’s relationship, which perhaps is why the musical lacks punch...
Dull and docile Eurydice and Orpheus are subsumed by the fuss and pizazz around them.

The thin narrative structure and minimal character development are not so much acted as felt in the expressive delivery of the songs...While not every aspect succeeds in presenting a cohesive story, its Broadway debut offers an innovative approach to the musical genre and an often electrifying experience in cutting-edge theater.
What previously felt otherworldly and jarring — a journey from a sweaty, smoky Southern bar straight into the bowels of hell — now comes across as overly Broadway-ified and occasionally pandering.
It’s music that’s alternately seductive, mesmerising and exhilarating, adjectives that, of course, describe the entire Hadestown experience.
“Hadestown” is a triumph of craft and imagination, boldly poetic, rousingly political, and vividly beautiful.
I cannot imagine there will be a better Broadway musical this season. Run.
This rare production thrums with poetic grace and ancient rhythmic currents that resonate profoundly, irrevocably with life.

Hadestown delivers a deeply resonant and defiantly hopeful theatrical experience, filled to overflowing with passion, artistry, and love, even as are hearts are crushed in the end by our human frailties.
It is both the most original and breathtaking musical of the season and a trenchant piece of political art.
Practically every single thing about “Hadestown” is perfect.
HADESTOWN is boldly distinctive, emotionally resonant and uniquely refined.
'Hadestown' is the best new musical I have seen in years...overflowing with rich, lively music.

One of the many miracles of Hadestown, Anaïs Mitchell and Rachel Chavkin's strange, stunning folk opera at the Kerr, is the richly bittersweet way it manages to simultaneously lament and celebrate the endless repetitions that make up human lives.
Under the direction of Rachel Chavkin, this stage brings a bright freshness to a classic tale and Hadestown is definitely a must-see for this season.
Hadestown now seems far more dramatically fleshed out than I remember, and many will be emotionally moved by its tragic story.
The rest of us will be grateful for the opportunity to enjoy something different.

Our Orpheus (Reeve Carney) is the sweetest and gentlest of souls who works in a café and Eurydice (Eva Noblezada) is a wandering waif who crosses Orpheus’ path and he falls madly in love with her. To narrate all that happens or will happen is Hermes (the remarkable Andre DeShields).
Now the show has taken up residence at the venerable Lyceum Theater and it’s even better.

cn.t: Critics hail this folk-opera retelling of the Orpheus myth as a thrilling, visually stunning triumph with a gorgeous score and superb cast, though a few find it emotionally distant. Most praise its timely political resonance and inventive staging.
